In case it helps, I also have this problem (PostgreSQL 11.8, Quarkus 1.5.1; everything works fine in Quarkus 1.4.2), in this method here: https://gerrit.benkard.de/plugins/gitiles/mulkcms2/+/60c0892466c8e48faba3e7bbe2b462c47aa032fa/src/main/java/eu/mulk/mulkcms2/benki/bookmarks/BookmarkResource.java#82

It only affects updates of existing entities, not the creation of new ones.

The strange thing about it is that when I run my application locally, in development mode, the transaction is done and the saving performed as expected, but in production (in a Docker container created with `quarkus-container-image-jib`) it is not.

Maybe something about how the code for change detection of bare field updates is generated at JAR build time has changed?  Pure speculation, though.

Sorry for not providing a better example.  I haven't gotten around to debugging it any further.

Some more observations:

- The bug occurs when running the JAR file created by `mvn package`, but not in development mode.
- `.isDirty()` on the Hibernate session is an indicator of the bug: When it occurs (and if there are no other changes in the session), `.isDirty()` returns false.
- If I use a setter instead of direct field access, `.isDirty()` returns true and the bug does not occur.  It still only saves the field set through the setter, not any of the other fields.

Generated code for direct field access:

Quarkus 1.4.2:

```
     aload         7
     aload         4
     invokevirtual #268                // Method eu/mulk/mulkcms2/benki/bookmarks/Bookmark.setDescription:(Ljava/lang/String;)V
```

Quarkus 1.5.1:

```
     aload         7
     aload         4
     putfield      #14                 // Field eu/mulk/mulkcms2/benki/bookmarks/Bookmark.description:Ljava/lang/String;
```
@benkard this helps a lot ! I'm pretty sure that with these information @FroMage will be able to understand what's going on !
